title: Stop the false STALL on merge --batch-build: the tool beats every 120 s, the watcher reads CPU time
why: Two false stalls (batch 138, batch 139 build 4) cost runner time and trust in the watcher.
source: Owner "B" 14:09 CST Nov 13 via the retrospective; ruling own-stall-beat-and-cpu-b.
note: Filed 14:10 CST Nov 13. Do both: (a) merge.py beats every 120 s in every phase via STALL_WATCH_BEAT, with a test that a silent batch-build phase draws no STALL; (b) the stall watcher reads the CPU time of the job's process tree, and a tree whose CPU time advanced in the quiet window is no stall. Rewrite decision stall-watch in place. Red cases: batch 138, batch 139 build 4. Keep the playwright lock-wait hang (no CPU) as a still-a-stall test. Retrospective's line numbers (merge.py 965, 1489, 1525 on main fccff95e6) are unread by triage. Cost of the CPU read goes in the record (reads per check) with a test, per outcomes-mechanize-rules.
